    A Menorca Farmhouse Finds Its Easy Elegance

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (830 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that above: In the living room, López-Quesada replicated the original ceiling beams and finished the walls in traditional Menorcan lime plaster.
    • According to recent reports, for Spanish designer Isabel López-Quesada, summers tend to revolve around Biarritz, in southwestern France, where she has a home.
    • Sources indicate that typically, López-Quesada goes there to relax and spend time with friends, but around five years ago she received a call from a Bilbao family who asked her to refresh their vacation home outside Mahón, Menorca’s capital.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that above: In the living room, López-Quesada replicated the original ceiling beams and finished the walls in traditional Menorcan lime plaster. A sofa of her design is grouped with a 1960s Tito Agnoli rattan daybed, a Mexican palm leaf stool, and a custom cocktail table upholstered with a Moroccan rug.

    According to recent reports, for Spanish designer Isabel López-Quesada, summers tend to revolve around Biarritz, in southwestern France, where she has a home. Still, she always carves out time for Menorca, regarded as the most laid-back of Spain’s Balearic Islands. That vibe suits the ELLE Decor A-list designer, whose signature style is luxurious but unfussy, harmonizing old and new with breezy refinement.

    Sources indicate that typically, López-Quesada goes there to relax and spend time with friends, but around five years ago she received a call from a Bilbao family who asked her to refresh their vacation home outside Mahón, Menorca’s capital. An old farm property, or finca, the five-bedroom residence required extensive updates. López-Quesada was steadfast in preserving such historical elements as a well and donkey stables, which she transformed into an indoor-outdoor bathroom with a patio and marble tub. “It was key to respect the style of Menorca,” she claims. “We were very careful with the materials, so it all goes together and conveys the sentiment I want the house to have.”.

    López-Quesada founded her namesake studio as a precocious 20-year-old Madrileña 40 years ago. Initially inspired by her mother’s yen for decorating and the work of celebrated Spanish designers such as Paco Muñoz and Fernando Benjumea, López-Quesada garnered wide attention in the early 2000s, when she converted an old Madrid wax factory into an atelier and a luxurious home for her family, filled with antiques and contemporary pieces. Soon she had interest from clients all over the world. Today López-Quesada’s 12-person team includes one of her three adult children, daughter Isabel Llanza. Five years ago the pair co-founded the lifestyle brand Isita Home, selling products they make themselves or discover on their travels.

    The Menorca project began by gutting the house’s interior and rebuilding it “in an old style,” López-Quesada claims. Central to it all was adding custom windows and doors to each room so the island’s golden light could flood the spaces. Vaulted and beamed ceilings were left intact or were recreated. Reconfiguring the floor plan, López-Quesada eschewed a proper dining room in favor of an eat-in open kitchen. “Most of the time you are eating outside,” she says.

    Recent findings suggest that with Menorca’s unrelenting summer sun, bougainvillea-draped pergolas were a must for leisurely alfresco lunches and dinners. Swaths of white lantana and lily of the Nile border the terraces, while “the pool reflects the sky like a mirror and provides a refreshing feel,” López-Quesada says.

    Her collaborator on the gardens was Spanish landscape architect Luis González-Camino. “My vision was to design a water-efficient Mediterranean garden, divided into distinct yet connected ‘garden rooms’ for different seasons and times of day,” he notes. González-Camino preserved the property as a natural Mediterranean woodland, with wild olive trees providing cover.

    Indoors, López-Quesada installed French terra-cotta floor tiles chosen for their aged look. The three fireplaces were all handcrafted in traditional Menorcan style—a little imperfect, painted white—and decorated with vintage tiles the designer keeps in her Madrid warehouse.

    Industry observers note that she offset the white ceilings and lime plaster walls with vibrant textiles and tilework in blues and greens inspired by Menorca’s native palette. An upstairs bedroom is anchored by an iron four-poster bed with a blue-and-white-striped canopy; its bath has a shower lined with lapis-colored zellige tiles. Doors, which across Menorca are customarily painted in bold shades, here are finished in verdant hues.

    Sources indicate that custom cabinets are designed with whimsically patterned cutouts for airflow, since humidity is a major factor. “On the islands, if you close the cupboards completely, mushrooms will grow inside,” López-Quesada indicates.

    Step Inside This Renovated Menorca Retreat.

    She arrayed the spaces with a lively mix of vintage and latest furnishings, emphasizing organic materials: rattan chairs, bamboo shades, Moroccan rugs, lots of linen and cotton fabrics in spirited florals or stripes. “If I use a heavy piece, then the rest is lighter,” she claims. The tableware maintains the blue and green theme, including pieces from Isita Home and hand-blown glassware from neighboring Mallorca.

    Industry observers note that in the end, the owners asked López-Quesada to redo their home in Spain’s Basque region as well. It’s one of several projects she right now has across the country, including reimagining a hotel in Barcelona, and she’s also designing homes in Paris, Shanghai, and the Dominican Republic. Many of her projects are with repeat clients. “That’s how it works,” the designer notes. “It’s like a chain.”.

    This story originally appeared in the November 2026 issue of ELLE Decor.

    Sarah Cristobal is a writer, editor, and creative consultant. She is currently editor-at-large for 10 Magazine USA, among other freelance projects.

    #89666. The Latest PlayStation Is 6 Years Old and Twice as Expensive as When It Debuted, What’s That About?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (929 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

    The Latest PlayStation Is 6 Years Old and Twice as Expensive as When It Debuted, What’s That About?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (929 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto VI is here, and it’s going to shock people heading into the holidays.
    • Do you have any idea how much a new entry-level PlayStation 5 costs now?
    • I’m imagining a guy—perhaps this is you, reader.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto VI is here, and it’s going to shock people heading into the holidays. No, we’re not moralizing about whatever violence, sex, or illegal activity is in the game. We’re talking about sticker shock.

    Do you have any idea how much a new entry-level PlayStation 5 costs now? It costs $600, yet it was only $400 when it debuted in 2020. And the entry-level Xbox? It’ll also run you $600, though you can get a model with less storage for $500. Also having rolled out in 2020, the lower-storage Xbox Series S used to retail for $300. Both those consoles are more than half a decade old, and they have increased in price by 50 percent.

    So what does a consumer do? I’m imagining a guy—perhaps this is you, reader. The last time he bought a console was a PlayStation 3 in 2013 for the previous Grand Theft Auto, or even a PS4 in 2018 for Red Dead Redemption 2. He thought about getting a PS5 for EA Sports College Football in 2024 but ultimately passed.This guy doesn’t pay attention to video games—or he only pays attention to the odd AAA release—and he is expecting to pay $400 for the key to experiencing this generation’s only game that matters. He might not even know that the game itself is going for $80, a rarity that only Nintendo has tried, with Mario Kart World. When he walks up to the counter, this hypothetical man will be paying nearly $900 to be able to play GTA VI. And the worst part? He’s not hypothetical. Starting Thursday, there are going to be thousands of real people in this very situation. Here’s why and what you can do—can you do anything?—about it.

    GTA VI has taken over a decade to make (that’s longer than it took Rome to build the Colosseum), and estimates put the budget somewhere north of $1 billion. Rockstar has pushed back, though, with head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe telling Bloomberg that the rumor of the budget surpassing the $1.5 billion budget of the Burj Khalifa is just that—a rumor. Still, it’s not a stretch to call this the biggest media release of all time.

    It’s also the biggest test of gaming’s resiliency to price hikes—price hikes that (like everything else, it seems) tie back to AI.

    “When [EA Sports College Football] came back a couple of years ago, there was an influx of people who hadn’t bought a console yet,” mentioned Mat Piscatella, a video game industry analyst and advisor at Circana. “Those folks at the time mostly chose either the Xbox Series S or the PlayStation 5 Digital, so the least expensive options to get in.”.

    It has been revealed that the main cause is that the multibillion-dollar gaming industry is in a crisis, a RAM crisis. The RAMageddon, or RAMpocalypse, is a global supply shortage of memory chips that is primarily caused by the post-2024 boom in generative AI. Cleanview, a market-intelligence organization, reported that the total number of data centers rose from 361 in 2016 to 1,278 in 2026, with more than five hundred more being built. Data centers are giant warehouses full of computer systems, complex computer systems requiring unprecedented amounts of RAM.

    RAM stands for random-access memory. Memory, in this instance, doesn’t mean storage space. RAM is your computer’s “short-term memory,” essentially how many different things your computer’s brain can process at once. The more RAM your computer has, the more it can handle simultaneously. And according to JP Morgan Global Research, prices have risen more than 400 percent in the past two years.

    Sources indicate that that gets us back to GTA VI and the world of video game consoles. Modern games, with their massive open worlds, highly detailed graphics, and complex physics simulations, require a ton of RAM. As computer parts become scarcer and more expensive, the price of a console goes up. Thus, consoles that—besides the higher-tier PlayStation 5 Pro—have not had meaningful updates in half a decade are now hundreds of dollars more expensive than they were at launch.

    Because contrary to what people know about the old gaming business models, the machines themselves still need to turn a profit. It didn’t use to be this way. In the PS2 era, consoles were sold at a loss, with games being the moneymaker. Things changed, audiences grew and moved elsewhere, and—somewhere between microtransactions and Xbox Game Pass—platform holders needed (or preferred) to make money on hardware again. So if a console is more expensive to manufacture, Sony and Microsoft aren’t going to eat that price. Consumers are seeing that increase directly, perhaps more directly and more acutely than we’ve ever seen any increase in technology prices.

    Sources indicate that here’s our advice: Don’t wait. The AI push shows no signs of slowing down, and it’s likely that this RAM pipeline bottleneck won’t fix itself for a year or two. This holiday season is getting underway with a supply and demand squeeze similar to what we saw in 2020, when these consoles originally released.

    According to recent reports, if you can swing it, you’ll probably want to buy a new console, but the PlayStation 5 Pro is already impossible to find brand-new. It might come down to shopping for renewed and refurbished consoles. These give you a very slight discount, but really they just give you a console that you can plug in and fire up GTA VI on. Welcome to the future of console gaming: refurbished six-year-old consoles.

    (Renewed) PlayStation 5 Digital.

    Industry News: Are Zen Hotels Now Putting Us to Sleep?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Above: One of the cottages at Little Saint in Healdsburg, CA.
    • Industry observers note that on the top floor of a Gilded Age McKim, Mead & White mansion in Latest York, now reincarnated as the Fifth Avenue Hotel, Martin Brudnizki recently put the finishing touches on a two-bedroom suite dubbed the Flâneur Penthouse.
    • Hotels in this vein tend to be -owner-operated properties looking to carve out a niche.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Above: One of the cottages at Little Saint in Healdsburg, CA.

    Industry observers note that on the top floor of a Gilded Age McKim, Mead & White mansion in Latest York, now reincarnated as the Fifth Avenue Hotel, Martin Brudnizki recently put the finishing touches on a two-bedroom suite dubbed the Flâneur Penthouse. With his hallmark exuberance, the Elle Decor A-List designer arrayed the space with distinctive flourishes: a spirited Scalamandré wallcovering trimmed in grosgrain ribbon, bespoke furnishings mixed with French Art Deco pieces, India-inspired inlaid nightstands, Japanese-style lamps, and Murano glass ceiling lights. Each element connects to an imagined narrative that shaped Brudnizki’s vision for the hotel: “this cinematic idea of the home of a flâneur who has traveled the world, has seen and acquired a lot, and put it together here,” the designer claims. “It’s a multicultural journey.”.

    Hotels in this vein tend to be -owner-operated properties looking to carve out a niche. One could trace a baroque family tree that links mold-breaking 1980s boutique hotels like Ian Schrager and Philippe Starck’s Royalton in Newly introduced York to Jacques Garcia’s interiors for the Hôtel Costes and L’Hotel in Paris to Ilse Crawford’s Ett Hem in Stockholm to Kelly Wearstler’s Proper Hotel in Austin.

    Fulk’s hospitality design, like Brudnizki’s, embraces spaces inspired by history and storytelling, with an emphasis on artistry, material richness, and character. Both men’s work is rooted in tradition, with idiosyncratic twists that feel fresh. And they have plenty of kindred spirits working in a diversity of styles, including such designers as Lorenzo Castillo, Kit Kemp, and Laura Gonzalez. While far from a coherent movement, the sumptuous, high-impact aesthetics practiced by these designers just might be today’s most zeitgeisty current.

    It has been revealed that take Fulk’s Cottages at Little Saint in Healdsburg, California, each one an elevated boho mashup of influences. “Sixties and ’70s rock and roll, and a sort of Laurel Canyon meets Northern California spirit,” explains the designer. “The cottages feel utterly like nowhere else.” And that, of course, is the point.

    Recent findings suggest that for his part, Brudnizki doesn’t care much for maximalism as a label. In the case of his glamorously moody interiors for the Broadwick Soho in London—shimmering surfaces, lavishly upholstered furnishings, a riot of pattern—everything began with an idea he describes as “Studio 54 meets your grandmother’s Soho townhouse, a disco granny kind of thing.”.

    It has been revealed that then there are the roughly dozen memorable properties created by Kit and Tim Kemp under their Firmdale Hotels group. The most recent is the Warren Street Hotel in New York, with the forthcoming Bedford Place Hotel slated to open next year in London next to the British Museum. “It’s about personality, a sense of arrival, and fun,” says Kit Kemp, who outfits each of her hotels with a more-is-more mix of her ebullient textiles and wallpapers in splashy colors, animated by art and craft.

    Sources indicate that kimberley Cohen, the creative director behind Maisons Pariente, claims her family’s small portfolio of hôtels de charme are about creating a residential-feeling experience that is also “something you have never seen, that you would not do in your own home.” She has worked with Brudnizki on Le Grand Mazarin in Paris, with Charles Zana on two hotels in the South of France, and with Pierre Yovanovitch on a Méribel chalet. Her latest project, opening this winter, is a Courchevel retreat named Saint Roch, with interiors by Friedmann & Versace that channel the chic romanticism of traditional dachas.

    Next up for Brudnizki, meanwhile, is the Knox Hotel, set to open soon in Dallas, newly introduced territory for him. As for what one should expect of the decor, he sums it up as “100 percent unapologetic glamour. It won’t be boring.”.

    As a woman who writes about men's fashion, guys I meet on dating apps love to ask me what jeans to buy—and I always recommend Levi’s. Specifically, Levi’s 505 jeans. “Not 501s?” one asked frantically. As Luke Guillory, Esquire’s commerce editor, poignantly noted in his Levi’s denim guide, the fit and materials of Levi’s infamous 501s have changed over the years, and “the most straightforward Levi's fit is not that straightforward, nor is it consistent across era.” By comparison, the slightly more modern 505 cut is a safer bet, especially when shopping online during Black Friday.

    “I prefer my jeans to hug up top, drape down low. A 505 does that,” Guillory wrote, declaring them Esquire’s pick for the best men’s jeans. “They're universally flattering and classic cut, so you don't have to worry about them going out of style. As a cheap pair of jeans go, it's the best way to go.”.

    Sources indicate that like many good things, Levi’s 505 jeans are on sale for Black Friday and Cyber Monday. This year, the brand’s entire site (minus a few exclusions) will be 40 percent off from November 23 to December 1, with early access starting November 19 for Red Tab Members. While you can find Levi’s markdowns at Amazon and other major retailers, you’ll find the widest range of washes, inseam lengths, and specialized fits by going straight to the source.

    Industry observers note that if you haven’t yet, it’s worth shopping Levi’s beyond jeans. The Sherpa Trucker Esquire editors have relied on for years now comes in a fresh corduroy fabric. For reliable workwear pants, try the rugged 568 Carpenter. And don’t sleep on Levi’s Classic Western Denim Shirt, which also makes a great gift.

    #89651. Movado’s New Tempo-Matic Watch Is Inspired by an Iconic Piece from the ’70s

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (278 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

    Movado’s New Tempo-Matic Watch Is Inspired by an Iconic Piece from the ’70s

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (278 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Movado was founded in 1881 in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, which isn’t a particularly odd backstory for a heritage Swiss watch brand.
    • Right now, a growing band of horological nerds is finding rich pickings in the Movado back catalog and pushing up vintage prices considerably—especially for its mid-century chronographs and its legendary Museum Watch (which celebrates 80 years in 2027; more of that to come) in the process.
    • In a recent development, it’s not only the collectors who are digging into Movado’s past, however.

    Movado was founded in 1881 in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, which isn’t a particularly odd backstory for a heritage Swiss watch brand. But it has been American owned since 1983 and has a distinct quality tied deeply to its long history in the U.S. market—which puts it slightly outside the predictable purview of many watch collectors.

    Right now, a growing band of horological nerds is finding rich pickings in the Movado back catalog and pushing up vintage prices considerably—especially for its mid-century chronographs and its legendary Museum Watch (which celebrates 80 years in 2027; more of that to come) in the process.

    In a recent development, it’s not only the collectors who are digging into Movado’s past, however. Last month, the brand released the Heritage Tempo-Matic ($995–$1,095), a re-creation of a watch that merges sporty and retro design in a neat and slinky package. The Tempo-Matic, Movado’s first automatic movement, was released in 1945 and went on to power a broad range of Movado’s wristwatches. But the rounded yet boxy “TV” shape of the latest Heritage Tempo-Matic is unmistakably 1970s, when watch design took a giant leap forward into sexy new territory.

    The 2026 version is available in three executions, each powered by the reliable Sellita SW200-1B movement and fitted with integrated steel bracelets that positively scream seventies. Two of them come in brushed steel with vertically brushed burgundy or blue dials. A third—which, we must admit, is our favorite—is gold-tone PVD with a warm gray dial. You’d be hard-pressed to find such an elegant, authentic, and affordable homage to the 1970s—a decade that’s at the moment a very hot motif in watch-collecting circles—anywhere else.

And the latest news on season 2 is that a certain cast member won’t be returning.

    “I’m not gonna be in the next season,” Riley Davis, who plays Allie’s ex-boyfriend Sean on the Prime Video series, told People at the New York City premiere of his movie November 1963 on November 18.

    What’s more: Riley’s exit could potentially signal that the second season of Off Campus might go a different direction from the book series it’s based on.

    As viewers saw in the show’s first season, Riley’s character, Sean, plays a pivotal role in Allie and Dean’s romance. In the books, he and Allie have an on-again, off-again relationship—but we might not see that pan out now that Riley is out.

    This isn’t the first time the TV adaptation shook things up with some changes from the source material. In season 1, the show’s writers introduced John Logan’s nonbinary sibling Jules Logan, who noticeably wasn’t in the OG book series.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that kate Middleton and Prince William have arrived in India for a three-day official visit, their first joint overseas tour since 2022.
    • It has been revealed that the couple will attend the awards ceremony on Tuesday, November 17, when five environmental initiatives will each receive £1 million to expand their work.
    • In a recent development, the royal itinerary extends beyond the ceremony.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that kate Middleton and Prince William have arrived in India for a three-day official visit, their first joint overseas tour since 2022. Revealed by Kensington Palace over the weekend, the November 16–18 trip is in honor of the sixth annual Earthshot Prize awards in Mumbai. It also marks a significant step in the Princess of Wales’s return to public duties following her 2024 cancer diagnosis.

    It has been revealed that the couple will attend the awards ceremony on Tuesday, November 17, when five environmental initiatives will each receive £1 million to expand their work. Founded by Prince William in 2020, the prize recognizes solutions across five areas, including restoring nature, reducing waste, and addressing climate change. Mumbai is the awards’ first Indian host city, following past editions in London, Boston, Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro.

    In a recent development, the royal itinerary extends beyond the ceremony. Kensington Palace said the visit would highlight sustainable urban transportation, responsible manufacturing, youth-led environmental projects, and India’s creative industries. Today, the couple joined cricket great Sachin Tendulkar and local children for a game of street cricket in Ballard Estate, a historic neighborhood in South Mumbai. The Prince and Princess of Wales are also scheduled to attend the inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards, recognizing environmental solutions developed by young people ages 9 to 17.

    The trip is Catherine’s first overseas tour with William since she disclosed her cancer diagnosis in 2024, and her first appearance at an Earthshot ceremony since the Boston awards in 2022. It is also the couple’s second official visit to India, a decade after their April 2016 tour.

    #89643. Who Is Daddy Franklin From ‘The Body’? For Starters, Nnamdi Asomugha Is Kerry Washington’s Husband

    Who Is Daddy Franklin From ‘The Body’? For Starters, Nnamdi Asomugha Is Kerry Washington’s Husband

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1084 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If you watched The Body in one sitting and are now fully obsessed with it, you’re not alone!!
    • In a recent development, though things got off to a rocky start (Kerry apparently told Nnamdi she didn’t date athletes, and Nnamdi told Kerry he didn’t date actors), the two got together anyway, and just about three years later in June 2013, they tied the knot in a super low-key ceremony.
    • Here’s everything you should know about the man behind Daddy Franklin, including how he rose to fame as a former NFL cornerback and what he’s up to next.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you watched The Body in one sitting and are now fully obsessed with it, you’re not alone!! The horrifying coming-of-age series is scary good, and while you may not be familiar with the actor who plays Father Samuel Franklin (aka Daddy Franklin), you definitely know his very famous wife. As it turns out, Nnamdi Asomugha has been married to Kerry Washington for over 13 years now, having fallen in love after watching Kerry perform in Race on Broadway in 2010. Kerry later confirmed the story during a 2018 interview with Marie Claire, saying, “The last time I did theater, it completely transformed my life. That’s where I met my husband.” Cute!!!

    In a recent development, though things got off to a rocky start (Kerry apparently told Nnamdi she didn’t date athletes, and Nnamdi told Kerry he didn’t date actors), the two got together anyway, and just about three years later in June 2013, they tied the knot in a super low-key ceremony. According to their marriage license, Kerry and Nnamdi said “I do” in Hailey, Idaho, where Nnamdi’s sister officiated and Kerry’s parents served as witnesses. Since then, the couple has welcomed two kids together—Isabelle Amarachi, born in 2014, and Caleb Kelechi, born in 2016—and are seemingly thriving outside of the spotlight. But we think it’s time to learn a lil bit more about Nnamdi, don’t you?

    Here’s everything you should know about the man behind Daddy Franklin, including how he rose to fame as a former NFL cornerback and what he’s up to next.

    Industry observers note that after growing up in Louisiana in a Nigerian Igbo household, Nnamdi attended the University of California, Berkeley, where he played for the California Golden Bears football team. Soon after graduating, Nnamdi was drafted in the first round of the 2003 NFL Draft by the Oakland Raiders, which is very impressive.

    Recent findings suggest that over his 11-year professional football career, Nnamdi also played for the Philadelphia Eagles and the San Francisco 49ers, and in December 2013, the cornerback signed a one-day contract with Oakland so he could retire as a Raider. I love to see a loyal man!

    According to recent reports, according to Nnamdi, the decision to retire at 32 was difficult, but it still felt like the right time for him. “Yeah, I felt that it was a good time, but it didn’t make it any easier,” he told UPROXX. “It’s a game that 'til this day I miss, and I miss playing. It’s not that I want to go play again, but I miss so many aspects of it; being around the team, being around the coaching, that calm before the storm.”.

    In a recent development, nnamdi first caught the acting bug all the way back in 2008, when he landed the role of “Party Guest with Wife” on the CW sitcom The Game. (Remember: There are no small roles, only small actors!!) He then caught the eye of director Peter Berg on the set of a Nike commercial shoot in 2009, who was impressed by the athlete’s ease in front of the camera. From there, Nnamdi went on to play small roles in Friday Night Lights, Leverage, and Cubed before making his on-screen feature film debut in 2012’s Fire with Fire.

    Since retiring from the NFL, Nnamdi has fully committed himself to his acting career with starring roles in the films Crown Heights, Sylvie’s Love, The Good Nurse, The Knife, and—most recently—The Body. He’s also served as a producer on several of those projects as well.

    Despite all his success, Nnamdi still remains as modest as ever, avoiding social media and press to instead focus on his craft. “I’m really bad at self-promotion. I know that about myself,” he previously explained to Bleacher Report back in 2017. “People told me all of the time, ‘You could be such a big star if you just talked about yourself more,’ but I’m not good at that. It’s always been about team.”.

    During a 2018 interview with Today, Kerry corrected a host when they alluded to her two children, saying, “I’m a mother of three." The reason: Nnamdi has a now-teenage daughter from another relationship, who Kerry has helped raise alongside her two biological children. And just like with Isabelle and Caleb, the couple keeps their eldest far from the paparazzi, so very little is known about her.

    As Kerry joked to People, “I have moments where I take pictures or videos of one of my three amazing kids and I wanna post it online, and I tend to just send it to my parents or my shrink instead.”.

    Philanthropy is notable to Nnamdi, which is why he created the Asomugha Foundation in 2005 at the very beginning of his career.

    The foundation has two main programs: Orphans and Widows in Need (which provides food, shelter, medicine, vocational training, literacy efforts, and scholarships to widows and orphans in Nigeria) and Asomugha College Tour for Scholars (which takes selected students from Bay Area and Los Angeles area high schools on college tours across the country).

    Though Kerry and Nnamdi are both actors and producers, it isn’t often that they work together on creative projects. Back in 2017, Nnamdi told Vanity Fair that it was possible he and his wife would co-produce a project at some point.

    “We would produce,” he said. “We’d probably produce before acting, I would think.” The following year, his production organization, iAm21 Entertainment, helped produce American Son, a Broadway play starring Kerry, and hopefully, that won’t be the last time the two are involved in the same project.

    In a recent development, as far as sharing the screen goes, however, Nnamdi doesn’t think that will ever happen. As he told The New York Times, “I produced American Son, but as actors, there’s no proposal as of now for that collaboration. We’re very supportive of each other’s journeys, but we’ve always been that way. We always want the best for each other in whatever we’re doing.”.

    According to recent reports, case in point? The couple’s *chef’s kiss* appearance at the 2025 Met Gala. Ahem:.

    Oh, and the duo’s 2025 Golden Globes looks:.

    Sources indicate that and ofc, he was right by Kerry's side during her December 2024 Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony, where she finally received her well-deserved star. How cute do they look with Kerry's parents??

    Industry observers note that TL;DR: Kerry and Nnamdi truly couldn’t be any cuter. Keep on being adorably low-key, you two.

    Tech Report: Ezra Sosa Called Out These ‘DWTS’ Pros for “Betting Against Him” in a Since-Deleted TikTok

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Though Ezra Sosa and his celeb partner, Julia Stiles, were eliminated after performing a paso doble to “Satisfied” from Hamilton on Dancing With the Stars’ Disney Night, the pro is still keeping up with the competition—and he seemingly called out some shady behind-the-scenes behavior from former DWTS pros.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Though Ezra Sosa and his celeb partner, Julia Stiles, were eliminated after performing a paso doble to “Satisfied” from Hamilton on Dancing With the Stars’ Disney Night, the pro is still keeping up with the competition—and he seemingly called out some shady behind-the-scenes behavior from former DWTS pros.

    After Tuesday night’s shocking results, Ezra posted—and later deleted—a TikTok where he wrote, “I wonder how much money some former pros have lost on Kalshi…”.

    Ezra seemingly slammed Maks Chmerkovskiy and Gleb Savchenko for placing bets against their fellow pros on Kalshi.

    “get them ezra, that behavior is so weird from former pros, they are such losers,” one fan wrote after a screenshot of his TikTok circulated on Reddit.

    Another pointed out that other former pros, including Sasha Farber and Peta Murgatroyd, have also placed online bets throughout season 35.

    “I hope that all the former pros betting on the show never get asked back in any capacity, even in the live audience,” they wrote. “It’s a massive conflict of interest and can actually sway voting patterns if Kalshi bets on dwts become more widespread and normalized. Maks, Gleb, Sasha, Peta I’m looking at you losers!”.

    However, someone chimed in with a valid point: “Unfortunately they’re not losing their own money (in fact they’re actually getting paid), they’re just trying to influence their followers to lose money on what should be an illegal app.”.

    Ezra isn’t the first person to call former pros out on their bets, either.

    During a November 18 interview with USA Today, Jan Ravnik made a pointed remark when asked to leave a message for his haters: “I hope you lose all your money.”.

    In a recent development, the day before that, Jan made a dig at Maks during a DWTS livestream when Brandon Armstrong and Alan Bersten commended him for his “beautiful” choreography. “Say that to Maks,” he said.

    This all comes after Maks and Gleb publicly shared their DWTS season 35 bets online, but Maks has long criticized Jan’s involvement on the show.

    He has since apologized to Jan, but still placed bets against him so…who even knows what’s going on.

    #89624. Has Zegna Cracked the Code to Modern Tailoring?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (774 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

    Has Zegna Cracked the Code to Modern Tailoring?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Pay attention to the world of menswear long enough, and you’ll notice that certain quandaries come up time and again.
    • According to Alessandro Sartori, the artistic director of Zegna for a little more than a decade now, there’s another question we should all be asking ourselves: What exactly is a suit these days?
    • Sources indicate that “Everything we do here is grounded in tailoring techniques and in tailoring fabrics,” Sartori tells me over Zoom from his home in Milan.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Pay attention to the world of menswear long enough, and you’ll notice that certain quandaries come up time and again. A favorite among traditionalists and avant-garde types alike is the fate of the suit. It’s been incorrectly declared dead enough times that the handwringing over its demise has largely shifted to questions of its evolving role in the modern guy’s wardrobe: Who wears a suit, and when, and why?

    According to Alessandro Sartori, the artistic director of Zegna for a little more than a decade now, there’s another question we should all be asking ourselves: What exactly is a suit these days?

    Sources indicate that “Everything we do here is grounded in tailoring techniques and in tailoring fabrics,” Sartori tells me over Zoom from his home in Milan. “But I'm a big believer that a suit doesn't necessarily have to be a combination of the classic top and the classic bottom in the same fabric and color.” It can be comprised of those things, he stresses. But the “modern suit,” as he calls it, can also be an intentional pairing of a different kind of top—a chore coat, an overshirt—with a trouser with a different fabrication. The materials and colors should feel complementary and cohesive but needn’t be perfectly matched.

    “This is not only a way to give a newly introduced life to suiting,” he explains, “but to dress men differently—and, at the same time, keep the quality, the craft, and the beautiful fit that a tailored piece has.”.

    The idea is to adapt classic techniques to the realities of getting dressed today. “Many fashion brands offer a nice quality, but is not the handmade quality that we do,” Sartori says. “And there are a lot of brands that are offering beautiful, beautiful quality, but they are quite classic.” Since he started in 2016, Sartori’s overarching project has been to populate the gulf between those two modes of production, making clothes that feel contemporary but are rooted in the top-tier fabrics and handwork that helped Zegna become the powerhouse of Italian fashion that it is today.

    The latest addition to Sartori’s lineup is a new jacket, the Falcon. It pays homage to the sort of utilitarian jackets Zegna founder Ermenegildo Zegna might have worn while walking the grounds of what is now the Oasi Zegna nature reserve in northern Italy, at the base of the Biellese Alps. (According to company lore, Ermenegildo imagined those walks as being accompanied by the flight of a falcon.).

    Sources indicate that sartori acknowledges that the use case, in 2026, might be a little different. “I don't think that people are necessarily using the jacket walking up in the mountains,” he claims. The Falcon is more about embracing a “sporty-chic attitude,” whether you’re stomping around the country or the city, and working within the modular framework that the designer has created at Zegna. You can mix and match it with other pieces—both old and upcoming—from the brand, and you can wear it as part of a “modern suit” or on its own.

    The new design is cut from Zegna’s Oasi Cashmere for lightweight warmth, and Sartori calls it “a great addition to our vocabulary.” Buttoned patch pockets give you somewhere to stash your stuff, a bowling collar can be flipped up to shield against stiff winds, and an internal drawstring can be cinched at the midsection for a little extra protection against the cold. Ultimately, it’s a familiar-looking piece. But it’s exceptional in its construction and materials and its design—a streamlined take on the hunting jackets of yore—is as considered as how it’s made.

    It has been revealed that “Long-lasting life is a key factor for what we're doing, and I don't mean only quality-wise,” Sartori says. “I also mean design-wise.”.

    The designer, for his part, hopes that the Falcon—alongside other modern classics from the brand—will be the sort of thing that guys wear and reinterpret for years before passing it on to the next generation. And as the brand continues to grow and evolve alongside its customer base, one of his biggest aims is to ensure that each item he introduces remains relevant throughout its (ideally long) lifespan.

    It has been revealed that “It’s like writing a book, and every season I add a chapter,” he notes. “Because the story is going on, is moving with our clients, our community of people, our brand, our family. So many layers are … I don’t want to say ready, but cooking. I see a bright future for the brand, following this principle of walking with our customers and building an indelible aesthetic. I like this approach.”.

    • The longtime Beverly Hills home of Warren Beatty and Annette Bening will soon hit the market, ELLE Decor can exclusively reveal.
    • The A-list actors parted with their longtime property in 2012, selling it for $6.7 million, per Zillow.
    • The nine-bedroom estate’s current owners—hotelier Jonathan Baker and his wife, Jenny—acquired the property directly from Beatty and Bening, then spearheaded a $5 million renovation that concluded in 2019.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The longtime Beverly Hills home of Warren Beatty and Annette Bening will soon hit the market, ELLE Decor can exclusively reveal. The married couple custom-built the gated residence in 1992 and raised their four kids there. The stars are one of Hollywood’s most famous power couples: Beatty has received 14 Academy Award nominations, winning for Best Director in 1982, and three Golden Globe Awards, while Bening has received five Oscar nominations, including Best Actress for 1999’s American Beauty, for which she won the Golden Globe.

    The A-list actors parted with their longtime property in 2012, selling it for $6.7 million, per Zillow. Its newly introduced asking price will be $14.995 million.

    The nine-bedroom estate’s current owners—hotelier Jonathan Baker and his wife, Jenny—acquired the property directly from Beatty and Bening, then spearheaded a $5 million renovation that concluded in 2019. They modified the Mediterranean-style home to have a more contemporary feel, with minimal moldings, glossy surfaces, modern furnishings, and bold splashes of color.

    However, they still paid homage to the estate’s movie-star pedigree, creating what they call the “Warren Beatty Theater,” a 17-seat screening room in what was once Beatty’s home office.

    According to recent reports, other nods to the legendary actor—who starred in classics like Bonnie and Clyde, Dick Tracy, and Bulworth—included integrating his drop-down projection screen into the new living room. Additional perks include a wine room with a suspended-wire storage system, a wood-paneled dressing room with plenty of built-ins, and a network of terraces.

    The home’s amenities continue on the manicured grounds, which feature an infinity-edge pool, a lighted tennis court, multiple al fresco entertaining areas, and a separate guest house.

    The couple are parents to four children, among them Ella Beatty, who is following in her parents’ acting footsteps and recently played Lizzie Borden in the Netflix series Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story.

    The Beverly Hills house will be listed for $14.995 million with Cory Weiss of Douglas Elliman and Jacob Greene of the Altman Brothers at Douglas Elliman.

    Geoffrey Montes is an associate editor at ELLE Decor with a serious love for all things real estate and design. Before that, he worked at Architectural Digest, Galerie, and Preservation magazines, covering everything from jaw-dropping listings to world-famous architects and design events like Salone del Mobile and Homo Faber.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor.
    • According to recent reports, you don't need a sprawling stone cottage in the Highlands, a sweeping countryside view, or a roaring fireplace to bring a little Scottish country-house charm into your home.
    • The secret is mixing those old-world details with pieces that feel fresh and livable, so your home doesn't end up looking like a period drama set.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

    According to recent reports, you don't need a sprawling stone cottage in the Highlands, a sweeping countryside view, or a roaring fireplace to bring a little Scottish country-house charm into your home. In fact, the appeal of this cozy, heritage-inspired aesthetic is that it can work just as beautifully in a city apartment as it does in a centuries-old estate.

    The secret is mixing those old-world details with pieces that feel fresh and livable, so your home doesn't end up looking like a period drama set. A tartan runner on the dining table, a cashmere throw draped over your favorite reading chair, or a few leather accents on the coffee table can bring just the right amount of countryside character to an otherwise modern space. Strathberry's new tartan homeware collection is another lovely entry point, giving the traditional pattern a contemporary spin that feels right at home in all kinds of interiors.

    Whether you're fully embracing your countryside daydreams or just looking to make your space feel a little warmer and more layered this winter, there are plenty of ways to bring the look home. Read on for the Scottish country-house-inspired touches that make this aesthetic so charming—and how to work them into your own space.

    If there's one pattern that deserves a starring role in a Scottish country-inspired home, it's tartan. And you don't have to limit it to a throw blanket or a few accent pillows. Designer Kaitlin Smith recommends “using plaid for a wallpaper or even as an accent pillow” to bring that distinctly Scottish feel into a space.

    Sources indicate that for a bolder take, try a tartan wallpaper in a powder room, entryway, or tucked-away reading nook. If you'd rather ease into the look, a single plaid pillow or upholstered accent piece can make just as much of a statement. With so many different tartan patterns and colorways to choose from, you can find one that brings a little heritage-inspired character to your home without making the whole room feel like a theme.

    A Scottish country house should feel like it's been lived in for generations, not styled within an inch of its life. That's where woven baskets come in.

    Sources indicate that noel Gatts, a designer and HGTV personality, recommends introducing “some slouchy woven baskets” throughout the home, whether at the entryway for shoes and umbrellas or in a living room or bedroom to hold extra blankets. Their slightly relaxed shape and natural texture add to that collected, lived-in feeling while giving everyday clutter somewhere to go.

    Try a larger basket beside the front door, a smaller one tucked under a console or an oversized version next to your favorite reading chair. It's a practical detail that also brings in the natural materials that make this aesthetic feel so grounded. Plus, having a cozy throw within arm's reach is never a bad idea.

    You can practically picture a pot of tea warming by the fire in a Scottish country house, and Gatts recommends leaning into that feeling with a thoughtful arrangement of crockery and candles.

    “Feature a fireplace or dining table with tea pots, earthenware, and an installation of candles and/or candlesticks,” she suggests. This is a lovely opportunity to bring out those pieces you might otherwise save for special occasions, from vintage teapots and handmade ceramic bowls to mismatched candlesticks and well-loved serving dishes. Grouping them together creates a charming focal point without making the space feel overly formal.

    Recent findings suggest that candlelight is especially important here, adding a soft, welcoming glow that feels worlds away from bright overhead lighting. And if you don't have a fireplace, a dining table, mantel or console can give you the same cozy effect.

    A Scottish country house shouldn't feel too coordinated, so don't be afraid to bring a few different patterns into the mix. As designer Sarah Cole suggests, “try pairing a wool plaid with a botanical print, a small geometric pattern or a traditional rug.”.

    In a recent development, the combination adds visual interest and gives a room that layered, lived-in quality that makes country-house interiors so inviting. You can keep the look cohesive by pulling a few warm, autumnal colors throughout the patterns—like russets, burgundies, forest greens and ochres—while varying their scale so they don't compete with one another. It's a simple way to make the space feel more personal and collected over time.

    According to recent reports, the Scottish country-house look has a wonderful appreciation for pieces that feel like they've been around awhile. Rather than filling every surface with brand-upcoming accessories, Gatts suggests bringing in “found objects with a sense of history” made from weathered wood, pottery, or patinated brass. These are the kinds of details that give a room its personality, whether it's an old wooden box on a coffee table, a vintage ceramic vessel or a brass object with a little wear and patina.

    According to recent reports, don't worry about everything matching, either. A mix of materials and finishes makes the space feel more authentic and less like you ordered the entire room in one shopping trip. Gatts recommends using these pieces on a coffee table for “the perfect antique flair,” but a bookshelf, sideboard, or entryway console would work just as well.

    Industry observers note that finally, a few well-chosen antique details can give a room that Highland lodge feeling without requiring a full redesign. Jill Wheeler of Birch Hill Interiors recommends adding “a touch of polished brass like antique candlesticks or wall sconces to give the space a refined look.” Try styling a pair of vintage brass candlesticks on a mantel, placing one on a coffee table, or swapping in brass wall sconces beside a favorite reading chair.

    Wheeler also suggests incorporating antiques on a mantel, coffee table, or built-in, noting that “antiques can help bring the outside in and tell a story.” The mix of aged finishes and meaningful finds adds a sense of history and character that makes a Scottish country-inspired space feel genuinely lived in.

Now, the madness is largely confined to the Internet—and the sales, like everything else, never actually stop.

    Case in point: Amazon’s 12-day Black Friday sale has officially landed a week before Thanksgiving, and with it comes some of the year’s best Apple prices, including impressive deals on AirPods. Every time Apple gadgets go on deep discount, they tend to sell out quickly. It’s just like those Black Friday mad dashes, just from the comfort of your own couch, so it would behoove you to shop sooner rather than later.

    Sources indicate that right now, both the AirPods Pro 3 and the AirPods Max 2 are hovering close to their lowest prices ever.     Chanel Chance Eau Splendide Is My Favorite of All the Chance Perfumes. Here’s Why I Love It So Much

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1202 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love.
    • My mom’s Chanel No.5, a fixture in our bathroom cabinet, was the first perfume I ever knew by name.
    • In a recent development, enter Chanel Chance Eau Splendide, the purple-hued 2025 addition to the brand’s beloved Chance fragrance collection.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

    My mom’s Chanel No.5, a fixture in our bathroom cabinet, was the first perfume I ever knew by name. It’s sophisticated and timeless, much like most of the other best-of-the-best Chanel fragrances that have been released since No.5’s 1921 debut. And while I have nothing but respect for the classics, I’ll admit that some of the brand’s more traditional floral fragrances aren’t necessarily what I reach for on a regular basis. I’m usually more interested in something a little fruitier, fresher, and more playful.

    In a recent development, enter Chanel Chance Eau Splendide, the purple-hued 2025 addition to the brand’s beloved Chance fragrance collection. With a sparkling raspberry opening, a heart of rose geranium, and a soft, musky base, it promises a bright, youthful take on the classic Chanel scent profile. And as someone who spends a considerable amount of time sniffing new perfumes for work, I know things are serious when they earn an immediate permanent spot on my vanity.

    In a recent development, after attending the launch event for Eau Splendide last April, I didn’t intend to make it my upcoming go-to... but that’s exactly what happened. I got an early sample, started wearing it, and simply noticed that I was reaching for it nearly everyday. I quietly fell in love with it as it sneakily became one of my signature scents. Now, after wearing it pretty consistently for a year and a half, here’s my honest review of Chanel Chance Eau Splendide Eau de Parfum, including what it actually smells like on skin, how it wears throughout the day, and whether it’s worth the luxury price tag. Ahead, everything to know before adding it to your fragrance collection.

    First things first: Chanel Chance Eau Splendide is a fruity floral, with a much brighter opening than you might expect from a traditional Chanel perfume. I’m not exactly surprised that I love it so much, given that fruity florals make up about 90 percent of my perfume collection.

    The fragrance features a raspberry top note that gives it a juicy, slightly tart fruity sweetness. But rather than leaning into the saccharine, sugary territory of some fruity perfumes, Eau Splendide then introduces rose geranium as a heart note, which adds a fresh, rosy, and surprising-but-subtle minty moment. To me, this is how you construct a perfect fruity floral: Before it gets too sweet (and for me, headache-y), some fresh floral notes balance everything out.

    Recent findings suggest that but that’s not all: As the fragrance dries down, you’ll experience base notes of iris, cedar, and white musk that make for a soft finish. To me, it results in a scent that feels elegant, feminine, and sophisticated—very Chanel—without being particularly heavy.

    Industry observers note that splendide is a fresh and light scent, but don’t think that means it’s not staying put on your skin throughout the day. It usually lasts about four to six hours on me, so while it’s certainly not the longest-lasting fragrance I own, about four spritzes of it gets me through most of the day.

    With so many great Chanel fragrances, how does this stand up against the rest? If I had to describe the overall vibe, I’d say that Chance Eau Splendide makes me feel effortlessly put together, but it also has a playful streak to it. I smell the raspberry most prominently on my skin, though, as it gets later in the day, I also notice the iris and musk. Even though I have dozens of fruity floral perfumes, it’s different than any of the others in my fragrance wardrobe.

    The first time I spritzed it, I did wonder if it was going to be too sweet for me. Ultimately, I found that the raspberry and rose geranium mix well together and don’t feel too sugary whatsoever. I also love how youthful it is, especially compared to some of the other Chanel fragrances out there. It’s super flirty, vibrant, and fresh, making it the perfect companion for daytime meetings, date nights, and more—I even wore it to Coachella this year. All in all, the one word I’d use to describe it is approachable. Is it the most complex perfume I’ve ever sniffed? No. But the scent, the vibe, and the longevity make it perfect for anyone from a first-time Chanel fragrance wearer (I think it’s a great introduction to the brand) to a fruity floral fanatic. For me, it’s an everyday bottle that takes me from day to night all year long.

    According to recent reports, on that last point: I can see why someone might call it a spring or summer perfume, given the notes. But there’s no rule that says you have to put away your fruity florals when temperatures drop. This is the kind of fragrance that works whenever I’m craving something bright and fresh.

    Chanel Chance Eau Tendre Eau de Parfum.

    Chanel Chance Eau Fraîche Eau de Parfum.

    Industry observers note that okay, so is Chanel Chance Eau Splendide actually worth the splurge? It’ll definitely be a re-purchase for me, and not just because it comes in a pretty purple bottle.

    Industry observers note that here’s my case for giving it a chance—yes, pun intended. The juicy raspberry opening is playful without veering into candy territory, while the other notes give it that effortlessly polished Chanel feel. It’s the kind of fruity floral that doesn’t need to be retired the second sweater weather arrives. I say we let this one live its best life all 12 months of the year.

    Recent findings suggest that of course, Chanel prices are Chanel prices (even the smallest bottle is $115), so I’d recommend giving it a test spray before committing to a full bottle—especially if you typically gravitate toward super-sweet gourmands or bold, spicy fragrances. But that being said, I’ve been wearing it regularly for well over a year and I’m nowhere near the end of my bottle, so it’ll last you a while. For anyone who loves a fresh, feminine scent with a little personality, Eau Splendide is definitely worth a sniff. That said, since it’s such an easy-to-wear, clean-meets-powdery-meets-sweet scent, I’d consider it a pretty safe blind buy if that sounds like the type of perfume you generally gravitate toward.

    I’ve worn this to weddings, concerts, dinners... You name it, you can wear this perfume there. She’s effortlessly versatile, isn’t overpowering, and isn’t a snob—even though she’s polished, there’s no intimidation factor, and she doesn’t take herself too seriously. She’s a must-have for anyone, whether you’re newly dabbling in fragrance or someone who already swears by a classic fruity floral. Consider this review my formal petition to add it to a list of all-time best year-round scents.

    Industry observers note that catharine Malzahn is a contributing beauty writer at Cosmo who covers all things beauty, including fragrance. For this story, she shared her experience wearing the Chanel Chance Eau Splendide Eau de Parfum, one of her go-to perfumes for year-round freshness.

    Catharine Malzahn is a contributing beauty writer at Cosmopolitan and was previously the beauty assistant at Good Housekeeping, Woman's Day, and Prevention.

    #89608. Why Am I Still Mad at My Partner After Makeup Sex?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1058 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cosmopolitan ↗ Open Full Page

    Why Am I Still Mad at My Partner After Makeup Sex?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1058 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, arguments with your partner typically follow a general sequence of events: Something upsets you.
    • But what if after your conversation and orgasm, you find yourself still upset with your partner?
    • Recent findings suggest that while I’m a firm believer that makeup sex is the best stamp of completion for every argument, this isn’t always the case for every relationship.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, arguments with your partner typically follow a general sequence of events: Something upsets you. You bring it up to your partner. You discuss (or argue). You go back and forth. You eventually work it out. You have wonderful makeup sex. And then—if the argument wasn’t super serious and you were able to hear each other out—you move on (give or take a few “I find it funny how...” monologues and a venting Facetime session with your best friend).

    But what if after your conversation and orgasm, you find yourself still upset with your partner? What if, even after putting the argument in the “done” pile, you feel lingering emotions of pain and anger?

    Recent findings suggest that while I’m a firm believer that makeup sex is the best stamp of completion for every argument, this isn’t always the case for every relationship. Sometimes you don’t realize that the argument hurt you deeper than you realized—and even a hot and heavy session can’t mask it.

    “While some couples experience sex as a bonding and often reparative experience, it may not solve the underlying process of disconnection or conflict in a relationship,” licensed marriage and family therapist Molly Mindel tells Cosmopolitan.

    She explains that while sex can be an incredibly powerful tool for connectedness and regulation, it can’t repair bigger challenges that may be at play—no matter how good the sex is.

    According to recent reports, you typically only have makeup sex... when you think you’re making up with your partner. And for many of us, we genuinely believe that’s the case when it happens. But sometimes, we get so caught up in the emotions and connectedness of the sex that we realize we actually don’t feel fully moved on from the argument.

    In a recent development, mandel explains that there are both physiological and psychological reasons sex can make us feel temporarily closer to our partner and less upset about whatever we were arguing about. .

    It has been revealed that “For one, sex temporarily changes our neurochemical and emotional states,” she states. She explains that oxytocin and dopamine are released during sex, which can make us momentarily feel really good and satisfied. But these chemicals don’t change our foundational relationship beliefs, unmet needs, or feelings about an argument.

    “Sex can also regulate ‘attachment distress,’ meaning we get very close and feel very secure temporarily to our partner (maybe even in ways we don't with them outside of a sexual interaction),” she explains. “But after sex is finished and we get back to our relationship, that sense of feeling understood or cared for or connected to can fade, which can cause emotional distress and alter our behavior in the relationship, bringing us right back to our regular cycle of conflict.”.

    Think of post-nut clarity. While we get swept up in our horniness, makeup sex is simply a band-aid that will typically fall off once the sex is over. And even mind-blowing sex is not enough to keep the illusion going.

    Sources indicate that it’s not just about the makeup sex. The makeup sex represents the finishing of an argument. And because you already talked about it (and f*cked about it) you should be completely over it, right?

    It has been revealed that well, not necessarily. You shouldn’t feel guilty about having unresolved feelings after an argument, especially if you didn’t feel like all of your concerns were addressed.

    “Lingering anger, resentment, and hurt days or weeks after an argument with your partner can be a normal part of conflict, and aren't always things we need to rush to ‘solve,’” Mandel states.

    Recent findings suggest that mandel explains that it’s common for people to want to leave conflicts with a sense of resolve—“almost as if we tied a nice bow on the conversation.” But our arguments, like our relationships, are never perfect. It’s less vital that an argument is resolved in a certain time period and more that both you and your partner feel heard, respected, and valued—no matter how long it takes.

    So if you feel mad even post-makeup sex, that’s totally normal.

    “It's worth reflecting on whether the lingering hurt is discomfort from the argument and disconnection, or if there's genuine lack of resolve around a serious concern or emotion needing attention,” Mandel suggests.

    Recent findings suggest that if the argument represents a larger pattern in the relationship, this may be the reason you still feel distress even after you “talked it out.” You may have discussed the specific instance, but still need to address the bigger issue at hand. Even if the argument was about something singular, sometimes you just feel like you haven’t fully noted your piece.

    Recent findings suggest that ”In relationships, conflicts are messy, complicated, and cannot be solved in a matter of moments,” Mandel indicates. “Usually, there is something left unsaid, a feeling that was left unaddressed, or one that comes up later, which can be uncomfortable and sometimes painful.”.

    Recent findings suggest that if your makeup sex didn’t seem to tie the argument together, you may be worried that nothing will. Don’t panic. Just because an argument leaves some lasting discomfort doesn’t mean that your relationship is doomed—it just means that you need to find a different method to approach the disagreement.

    “Sometimes the powerful and healthy thing to do is to say, ‘We may not resolve this entirely’ and ‘Can we learn to be okay with that open ended-ness together for now?’”.

    In a recent development, and from there, you have to work with your partner to figure out how to move forward. Mandel suggests revisiting the conversation when both partners are calm and emotionally available. This way, she says, both parties will be able to approach the issue with curiosity rather than blame.

    According to recent reports, like any argument, it’s going to take a lot of communication and then checking in after the fact. Just keep reminding yourself that there actually is no linear path to resolving conflict. And if both people prioritize each other during a discussion, there’s almost always a way through—even if it does take a few more conversations than expected.

    The good news, though? Once the argument really is resolved, and you leave feeling heard and attended to, there’s always more makeup sex to look forward to.
